subject: Constant of proportionality for detection function

messages.author: 31e2049957f9d695
messages.subject: Constant of proportionality for detection function
parts:
Dear all,=20

I'm doing a simulation study and try to thin a Log-Gaussian Cox Process =
using
the detection function which I fitted to the data from my field work.
The detection function is the half normal key + cosine series expansion, =
i.e.
g(y) is proportional to key(y)*(1+series(y)) (Buckland et al. 2001, Eq.
2.25).

My idea was to use 1 / key(0)*(1+series(0)) as constant of =
proportionality,
but I found that this is not the way it is done in DISTANCE.

My problem is, that I do not find an explanation how the constant of
proportionality is calculated in DISTANCE. Maybe someone can tell me how =
it
is done?!


Best regards,=20
Tim =20

messages.author: 1fb54f491646a589
messages.subject: Re: Constant of proportionality for detection function
parts:
Tim, as Distance uses maximum likelihood estimation, you need to work with =
the probability density function, not the detection function. The constant=
is then determined by ensuring that the pdf integrates to one. However, i=
f you want the estimated detection function for line transect sampling, you=
simply rescale the fitted pdf, so that the function equals 1 at y=3D0 - wh=
ich is equivalent to what you say. So if you have the fit of key(y)*(1+ser=
ies(y)), rescaling your way will give the fitted detection function. For p=
oint transect sampling, this doesn't work though, as the pdf and detection =
functions have different shapes. (The pdf is proportional to y times the d=
etection function.)

If this doesn't answer your query, perhaps we can sort it off the list?

Steve Buckland
